source_text: Ὑπόδειγμα δ’ ἡμῖν κατὰ παραδρομὴν ἐκκείσθω εἰς σαφήνειαν γνωστικὴν ἡ δεκάλογος. καὶ ὅτι μὲν ἱερὰ ἡ δεκάς, παρέλκει λέγειν τὰ νῦν. εἰ δὲ αἱ πλάκες αἱ γεγραμμέναι ἔργον θεοῦ, φυσικὴν ἐμφαίνουσαι δημιουργίαν εὑρεθήσονται· δάκτυλος γὰρ θεοῦ δύναμις νοεῖται θεοῦ, δἰ ἧς ἡ κτίσις τελειοῦται οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς, ὧν ἀμφοῖν αἱ πλάκες νοηθήσονται σύμβολα. θεοῦ μὲν γὰρ γραφὴ καὶ εἰδοποιία ἐναποκειμένη τῇ πλακὶ δημιουργία τοῦ κόσμου τυγχάνει. ἡ δεκάλογος δὲ κατὰ μὲν οὐράνιον εἰκόνα περιέχει ἥλιον καὶ σελήνην, ἄστρα, νέφη, φῶς, πνεῦμα, ὕδωρ, ἀέρα, σκότος, πῦρ. αὕτη φυσικὴ δεκάλογος οὐρανοῦ. ἡ δὲ τῆς γῆς εἰκὼν περιέχει ἀνθρώπους, κτήνη, ἑρπετά, θηρία καὶ τῶν ἐνύδρων ἰχθύας καὶ κήτη, τῶν τε αὖ πτηνῶν ὁμοίως τά τε σαρκοβόρα καὶ τὰ ἡμέρῳ χρώμενα τροφῇ, φυτῶν τε ὡσαύτως τὰ καρποφόρα καὶ ἄκαρπα. αὕτη φυσικὴ δεκάλογος γῆς. καὶ ἡ κιβωτὸς δὲ ἡ ταῦτα περιειληφυῖα ἡ τῶν θείων τε καὶ ἀνθρωπίνων γνῶσις εἴη ἂν καὶ σοφία. τάχα δ’ ἃν εἶεν αἱ δύο πλάκες αὗται δισσῶν προφητεία διαθηκῶν. ἀνεκαινίσθησαν οὖν μυστικῶς, πλεοναζούσης ἀγνοίας ἅμα καὶ ἁμαρτίας. δισσῶς, ὡς ἔοικεν, γράφονται δισσοῖς πνεύμασιν ἐντολαί, τῷ τε ἡγεμονικῷ τῷ τε ὑποκειμένῳ, ἐπεὶ ἡ σὰρξ ἐπιθυμεῖ κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα κατὰ τῆς σαρκός. ἔστι δὲ καὶ δεκάς τις περὶ τὸν ἄνθρωπον αὐτόν, τά τε αἰσθητήρια πέντε καὶ τὸ φωνητικὸν καὶ τὸ σπερματικὸν καὶ τοῦτο δὴ ὄγδοον τὸ κατὰ τὴν πλάσιν πνευματικόν, ἔνατον δὲ τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν τῆς ψυχῆς καὶ δέκατον τὸ διὰ τῆς πίστεως προσγινόμενον ἁγίου πνεύματος χαρακτηριστικὸν ἰδίωμα. ἔτι πρὸς τούτοις δέκα τισὶν ἀνθρωπείοις μέρεσι προστάσσειν ἡ νομοθεσία φαίνεται, τῇ τε ὁράσει καὶ ἀκοῇ καὶ τῇ ὀσφρήσει ἁφῇ τε καὶ γεύσει καὶ τοῖς τούτων ὑπουργοῖς ὀργάνοις δισσοῖς οὖσι, χερσί τε καὶ ποσίν· αὕτη γὰρ ἡ πλάσις τοῦ ἀνθρώπου. ἐπεισκρίνεται δὲ ἡ ψυχὴ καὶ προσεισκρίνεται τὸ ἡγεμονικόν, ᾧ διαλογιζόμεθα, οὐ κατὰ τὴν τοῦ σπέρματος καταβολὴν γεννώμενον, ὡς συνάγεσθαι καὶ ἄνευ τούτου τὸν δέκατον ἀριθμόν, δἰ ὧν ἡ πᾶσα ἐνέργεια τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπιτελεῖται. τῇ τάξει γὰρ εὐθέως γενόμενος. ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἀπὸ τῶν παθητικῶν τὴν ἀρχὴν τοῦ ζῆν λαμβάνει. τὸ λογιστικὸν τοίνυν καὶ ἡγεμονικὸν αἴτιον εἶναί φαμεν τῆς συστάσεως τῷ ζῴῳ, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῦ τὸ ἄλογον μέρος ἐψυχῶσθαί τε καὶ μόριον αὐτῆς εἶναι. αὐτίκα τὴν μὲν ζωτικὴν δύναμιν, ᾗ ἐμπεριέχεται τὸ θρεπτικόν τε καὶ αὐξητικὸν καὶ καθ’ ὅλου κινητικόν, τὸ πνεῦμα εἴληχεν τὸ σαρκικόν, ὀξυκίνητον ὃν καὶ πάντῃ διά τε τῶν αἰσθήσεων καὶ τοῦ λοιποῦ σώματος πορευόμενόν τε καὶ πρωτοπαθοῦν διὰ σώματος· τὴν προαιρετικὴν δὲ τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν ἔχει δύναμιν, περὶ ἣν ἡ ζήτησις καὶ ἡ μάθησις καὶ ἡ γνῶσις. ἀλλὰ γὰρ ἡ πάντων ἀναφορὰ εἰς ἓν συντέτακται τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν καὶ δἰ ἐκεῖνο ζῇ τε ὁ ἄνθρωπος καί πως ζῇ.
thought_title: The Decalogue as a Symbol of Creation
pass_a_gloss: Let the Decalogue be set forth as an example for us, by way of a sidestep, for clear knowledge. And that the ten is sacred, it remains to say these things now. But if the written tablets are a work of God, they will be found to show natural creation, for the finger of God is considered the power of God, through which the creation of heaven and earth is completed, of which both the tablets will be thought symbols. For the writing and shaping of God, left behind on the tablet, is the creation of the world. The Decalogue, however, contains according to the heavenly image, the sun and the moon, stars, clouds, light, spirit, water, air, darkness, fire. This is the natural Decalogue of heaven. And the image of the earth contains humans, animals, reptiles, beasts, and of the aquatic, fish and sea monsters, and of the birds, similarly, the flesh-eaters and those that use food by day, and of plants, likewise, the fruit-bearing and the unfruitful. This is the natural Decalogue of earth. And the ark, which contains these things, would be the knowledge and wisdom of divine and human things. Perhaps these two tablets would be the prophecy of two covenants. They were renewed, therefore, mystically, because of the abundance of ignorance and sin at the same time. It seems that the commands are written twice, with two spirits, with the ruling and the subject, since the flesh desires against the spirit and the spirit against the flesh. There is also a certain ten concerning the human himself, the five senses and the vocal and the seminal, and this, the eighth, is the spiritual according to the formation, and the ninth is the ruling of the soul, and the tenth is the characteristic of the Holy Spirit, which is added through faith. Besides these, the legislation seems to command ten human parts, sight and hearing and smell and touch and taste, and the two organs that serve them, hands and feet, for this is the formation of the human. The soul is also inserted and the ruling part is added, by which we reason, not born according to the casting of the seed, so that the tenth number is gathered even without this, through which the whole activity of the human is completed. For the human, being directly in order, takes the beginning of life from the passive. We say, therefore, that the rational and ruling part is the cause of the constitution of the animal, but also of the irrational part being ensouled and being a part of it. The spirit, therefore, has taken the vital power, by which the nourishing and growing and, in general, moving are enclosed, the bodily spirit, which is quick-moving and goes through all the senses and the rest of the body, and is affected first through the body. The ruling part, however, has the power of choice, concerning which there is investigation and learning and knowledge. But since the reference of all things is to one, the ruling part is constituted, and through it the human lives and lives in some way.

choices.why: the ruling part of the soul is meant

pass_b_english: Let the Decalogue be set before us as an example, by way of a brief digression, for the sake of clear knowledge. That the Ten is sacred need not be stated at this point. But if the written tablets are a work of God, they will be found to reveal a natural creation; for the finger of God is understood as the power of God, through which the creation of heaven and earth is completed, and both tablets will be recognized as symbols of the two realms (Exodus 31:18; Deuteronomy 9:10). The writing and shaping of God, inscribed on the tablet, constitutes the creation of the world. The Decalogue, in its heavenly image, contains the sun and moon, stars, clouds, light, spirit, water, air, darkness, and fire. This is the natural Decalogue of heaven. The earthly image, by contrast, contains humans, cattle, reptiles, wild beasts, and among aquatic creatures, fish and sea monsters; likewise among birds, both the flesh-eating and those that feed by day; and among plants, both the fruit-bearing and the unfruitful. This is the natural Decalogue of earth. The ark that encloses these things would be the knowledge and wisdom of things divine and human. Perhaps these two tablets represent the prophecy of two covenants. They were therefore renewed mystically, as ignorance and sin abounded together. It appears that the commandments are written twice, by two spirits, for the ruling part and the subject part, since the flesh desires against the spirit and the spirit against the flesh. There is also a certain tenfold structure within the human person himself: the five senses, the faculty of speech, the seminal faculty, and this—eighth—is the spiritual faculty according to formation; ninth is the ruling faculty of the soul; and tenth is the characteristic mark of the Holy Spirit, which comes through faith. Beyond these, the legislation seems to command ten human parts: sight, hearing, smell, touch, taste, and the two pairs of organs that serve them—hands and feet; for this is the formation of the human. The soul is then inserted, and the ruling part is added, by which we reason; this is not born at the casting of the seed, so that the number ten is complete even without it, and through these the whole activity of the human person is fulfilled. For the human, coming directly into being in due order, receives the beginning of life from the passive elements. We therefore affirm that the rational and ruling part is the cause of the animal's constitution, but also of the irrational part being ensouled and becoming a part of it. The bodily spirit, then, receives the vital power, which encompasses the nutritive, augmentative, and generally motive functions; it is swift-moving, traversing all the senses and the rest of the body, and suffers first impact through the body. The ruling part, however, possesses the power of choice, about which lies inquiry, learning, and knowledge. But since the reference of all things is gathered into one, the ruling part is constituted, and through it the human lives and lives in a certain way.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex theological and physiological structure described by Clement. Pass A preserves the sense of all clauses, and Pass B provides a more polished rendering that remains faithful to the Greek. The scripture citations added in Pass B (Exodus 31:18; Deuteronomy 9:10) are appropriate identifications of the allusions to the finger of God and the tablets.

The translation accurately reflects the Greek text, with appropriate citations and terminology. The Pass A and Pass B translations are consistent with the source, and the notes provide relevant biblical references. The title accurately represents the content of the passage.
